MANU/DE/3212/2012, decided on 23.04.2012, Hon'ble High Court of Delhi, set aside the order,
whereby recovery rights were granted to the Insurance Company, in the absence of valid fitness certificate.

to substantiate the said defence by leading any positive evidence and since, as per criminal case record also, Section 56/192A of M.V. act, was added, only on the ground that the owner failed to produce fitness certificate thus, it can be safely concluded that R3 failed to prove any breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy by R1 and R2, as such, they are not entitled to seek Ram Vati And Ors vs Dinesh Kumar And Ors on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102872587/
17 recovery rights, from the insured or from R1.
58.
Since there is no other statutory defence, on behalf of insurance company/R3, and as the offending vehicle was duly insured with R3, at the time of accident, therefore, R3 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners.
